_about: The one place GenClass plans are defined. telemetry-worker/src/plans.ts imports this file (limits, entitlements, Stripe lookup keys, the billing page) and site/build.py reads it (the pricing page). scripts/stripe-setup.mjs creates the Stripe products and prices from it. Everything GenClass makes is free: the runtime, its on-device model, the dashboard for every app with a year of history, export, forwarding, the page check and the closed-loop MCP server, which anyone can run on their own machine. What costs money is running the closed-loop MCP for you: Individual hosts it on genclass.dev, Enterprise runs it inside the customer's own network, by arrangement. `sale` says how a plan is had: free (install it), stripe (bought by card on genclass.dev/account/billing), contact (a person from GenClass arranges it; no Stripe, no card price). `on_sale` false keeps a stripe plan off sale everywhere (the site shows its price with an inactive button, the worker refuses its checkout and its trial) until what it sells has shipped; the hosted MCP has not, so Individual is not on sale yet. Prices are US cents; null means no card price (contact plans) or no yearly option yet. limits.apps null means no plan limit (the worker still caps an account at 200 apps against abuse). A trial gives Individual's entitlements for trial_days days, once per account, without a card: site/build.py reads trial_days for the public copy, the telemetry worker reads TRIAL_DAYS in telemetry-worker/wrangler.toml, and a telemetry-worker test checks that they agree. Feature lines with available false are shown as coming next. stripe_tax_code is the Stripe product tax code scripts/stripe-setup.mjs sets on the plan's product; managed_payments true sells the plan through Stripe Managed Payments (Stripe, through Link, is the merchant of record; only for fully automated digital products, so only Individual; telemetry-worker/README.md, Paid plans).
footer: Need the closed-loop MCP inside your own network, SSO or invoices? Email mehar@daybot.ca.
